parameters.content:
## Client onboarding V1
Form → Sheet row → Drive folder → Gmail alert.

Read left to right. Every node maps to one step in the reference implementation at github.com/uusammmaa/client-onboarding-automation, and to one module in make/blueprint.json.

**Before you run it:** set the four values in *Settings* (node 2), and connect the Google and Gmail credentials on nodes 4, 5, 7, 8, 9 and 10.

nodes.name: Note: the row is what matters

parameters.content:
### From here on, failures do not stop the run
The Sheet row already exists, so the client is on the tracker.

Drive and Gmail nodes are set to **continue using the error output**. A Drive outage leaves a client with no folder — a five-second fix. Rolling the row back would leave a client nobody knows about.

nodes.name: Settings
nodes.notes: The only node you edit to point this at a different account.

nodes.name: Reject with the reasons

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ok: false, error: 'That submission is not valid', problems: $json.problems }) }}

nodes.notes: 400, with the field names. The form should have caught these.

nodes.name: Read the tracker
nodes.notes: Needed to work out the next client ID. alwaysOutputData is on so an empty tracker still produces an item.

nodes.name: Add row to tracker
nodes.notes: THE step that must not be lost. Retries three times; a failure here stops the run and the client is told to try again.

nodes.name: Create client folder
nodes.notes: Not fatal. A client with a row and no folder is a five-second fix.

nodes.name: Create subfolders
nodes.notes: Runs once per item from the previous node.

nodes.name: Write the folder link
nodes.notes: Matches on Client ID, so it is safe to re-run.

nodes.name: Email the studio

nodes.notes: Reply-To is the client, so hitting reply answers them rather than the studio.

nodes.name: Log the failure

value.What to do: Check the node's credentials and the IDs in Settings, then re-run this execution from the failed node.

nodes.notes: Best effort. If the Sheet is what is broken, this fails too — which is why the email below does not depend on it.

parameters.subject: =Onboarding step failed · {{ $('Assign a client ID').first().json.clientId }}

nodes.name: Still confirm to the client

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ok: true, clientId: $('Assign a client ID').first().json.clientId, message: 'Thanks — we have your brief and will be in touch within one working day.' }) }}

nodes.notes: The client's brief was saved. What failed is internal, so they get the same confirmation.
